suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-19 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited systematic review and meta-analysis reported that a history of allergic rhinitis is strongly associated with increased risk of asthma. Require documented allergic rhinitis and separately established asthma before presenting the relationship; the cited systematic review and meta-analysis reported that a history of allergic rhinitis is strongly associated with increased risk of asthma, consistent with the united-airway/allergic-march concept, without establishing that allergic rhinitis caused an individual's asthma. Preserve other asthma triggers (viral infection, occupational exposures, exercise, irritants, gastroesophageal reflux) and other rhinitis phenotypes (non-allergic, vasomotor, mixed) as competing explanations. Do not infer asthma from rhinitis symptoms, spirometry in isolation, or self-reported wheeze alone. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
